intro: に比べて (にくらべて) sets up a yardstick. The noun before it is the reference point, and the rest of the sentence says how the subject measures up against it: hotter, cheaper, more people. It comes from the verb 比べる, to compare, so it always means a real comparison of degree.

skills.rule: [reference] に比べて、[subject] は [degree]: compared with X; X is the yardstick, not the thing being described.
skills.explain:
に比べて follows a noun, or a clause + の, that serves as the reference: 去年に比べて, 東京に比べて, 一人で勉強するのに比べて. The subject being described carries は or が, and the predicate gives a degree: 暑い, 安い, ずっと上手だ, or a change such as 増えた and 減った. と比べて means the same. に比べると and に比べたら are spoken variants ('if you compare'); に比べ is formal written style.

より is plain 'than' and attaches straight to the comparison: 今年は去年より暑い. に比べて says the same thing with the yardstick set up as its own phrase, usually at the front, and sounds a little more deliberate: 十年前に比べて観光客が増えた.

The edge: に対して also appears in contrasts, but it sets two facts side by side ('whereas') or names a target. In everyday sentences it is not a yardstick: 去年に対して今年は暑い is wrong. (Report figures such as 前年に対して五%増 are a fixed business usage.)
patterns: [time in the past] に比べて、[thing] が [増えた / 減った]
[clause] の に比べて、[subject] は [adjective]

examples.jp: 去年[きょねん]{に比[くら]べて}、今年[ことし]の夏[なつ]は暑[あつ]いです。
examples.en: This summer is hotter than last year's.

examples.jp: 都会[とかい]{に比[くら]べて}、田舎[いなか]は空気[くうき]がきれいです。
examples.en: Compared with the city, the air in the countryside is clean.

examples.jp: 兄[あに]{に比[くら]べて}、弟[おとうと]はよく食[た]べます。
examples.en: Compared with his older brother, the younger one eats a lot.

examples.jp: 十年前[じゅうねんまえ]{に比[くら]べて}、この町[まち]の人口[じんこう]はずいぶん減[へ]りました。
examples.en: Compared with ten years ago, this town's population has fallen a lot.

examples.jp: 電車[でんしゃ]で行[い]くの{に比[くら]べて}、バスは時間[じかん]がかかりますが安[やす]いです。
examples.en: Compared with going by train, the bus takes longer but is cheaper.

contrast.note: より is a bare 'than' tied to a comparative predicate (AはBより高い). に比べて says the same with a separate 'compared with X' frame, often placed first. Both work with change verbs (去年より増えた, 去年に比べて増えた).
に対して aims an attitude at a target or contrasts two facts (兄が静かなのに対して、弟はよく話す). It cannot be the yardstick of a degree comparison.
について means 'about' and compares nothing: 去年について話す is 'talk about last year'.

mistakes.bad: 去年[きょねん]{に対[たい]して}、今年[ことし]は雪[ゆき]が多[おお]いです。
mistakes.good: 去年[きょねん]{に比[くら]べて}、今年[ことし]は雪[ゆき]が多[おお]いです。
mistakes.note: A yardstick for 'more snow' takes に比べて.

mistakes.bad: 去年[きょねん]{くらべて}、今年[ことし]は雪[ゆき]が多[おお]いです。
mistakes.good: 去年[きょねん]{に比[くら]べて}、今年[ことし]は雪[ゆき]が多[おお]いです。
mistakes.note: The に (or と) cannot be dropped: に比べて or と比べて.

skills.tip: Is X the measuring stick in 'compared with X, ...'? Then に比べて. If it is 'whereas', it is に対して.
